title: Amion Alternative | We Build It, You Keep Amion
description: Amion alternative for GME programs? Scheduling Wizard is a managed service that builds the schedule for you.
h1: Amion Manages Your Schedule. We Build It.
paragraph: Keep Amion for the day to day. Scheduling Wizard builds the schedules built to the ACGME requirements you upload to it, no migration, no software to learn.

cta.title: Ready to Hand Over the Build?
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Amion is a schedule publishing platform, while Scheduling Wizard is a managed service that creates and optimizes the schedule itself. Many Scheduling Wizard clients continue using Amion to publish their finished schedules day-to-day. The difference is in schedule creation: Our team builds your compliant Block, Call, Clinic, and Attending schedules from your rules, then delivers them as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you you can upload directly to your existing platform.
faq.question: What makes Scheduling Wizard different from Amion?

faq.answer: No. Scheduling Wizard and Amion serve different functions and work together. Scheduling Wizard handles schedule creation and optimization. Your finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you that you can upload to your existing platform for day-to-day staff viewing, exactly as you do today. You keep your existing Amion workflow for publishing while Scheduling Wizard handles the build.
faq.question: Do I have to stop using Amion if I work with Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: The ACGME duty hour rules are applied as the schedule is built rather than audited afterwards: the 80-hour weekly limit, eight hours off between duty periods, the 24-hour cap, and the subspecialty-specific rules for your program. We work from the requirements your program tells us apply, and we redraft when something needs to change.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard ensure ACGME compliance during schedule creation?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard operates as a fully managed service, meaning your program does not need to operate any scheduling software. You submit your rules, rotation requirements, resident preferences, and ACGME rules. Scheduling Wizard's team handle the optimization and deliver finished, ready-to-publish schedules as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. Chief residents are not required to learn or use any new platform.
faq.question: Who actually builds the schedule with Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates Block (rotation), Call, Clinic, and Attending schedules. These are optimized simultaneously so that changes in one schedule automatically reflect across the others, removing the cross-schedule conflicts that arise when each schedule is built in isolation. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you compatible with your existing platform, and other publishing platforms.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate?

faq.answer: Your program's scheduling knowledge stays with Scheduling Wizard year over year. Rules, rotation rules, coverage requirements, and compliance configurations all persist in the system. When a new chief rotates in, they inherit an already-working, optimized setup instead of starting from scratch. This institutional continuity is a core reason programs choose Scheduling Wizard over rebuilding manually each year.
faq.question: What happens to our scheduling setup when a new chief resident takes over?
